metadata.name: Gastritis / functional dyspepsia (upper GI inflammation)
metadata.emergency_level: Routine - but GI bleeding or alarm features need urgent work-up
metadata.severity: Usually mild; can cause bleeding/erosions; overlaps with peptic ulcer and dyspepsia

overview.short_description: Inflammation/irritation of the stomach lining causing upper abdominal (epigastric) discomfort, nausea and bloating; commonly related to Helicobacter pylori or NSAIDs, and managed as part of the dyspepsia pathway.
overview.detailed_description: In primary care, gastritis and dyspepsia overlap and are managed together. Most patients without alarm features are treated with a 'test and treat' approach for H. pylori and/or a proton-pump inhibitor, reserving endoscopy for alarm features or treatment failure. The key safety task is to detect upper GI bleeding and features suggesting malignancy.
overview.pathophysiology: Mucosal injury/inflammation from H. pylori infection, NSAIDs/aspirin, alcohol, bile reflux or stress reduces mucosal defence and can cause erosions; H. pylori also drives chronic gastritis and peptic ulceration.
overview.etiology: Helicobacter pylori (common), NSAIDs/aspirin, alcohol, bile reflux, severe physiological stress (critical illness), autoimmune (pernicious anaemia), and rarely other causes.
overview.incubation_period: Not applicable (H. pylori infection is often long-standing).
overview.natural_history: Often chronic/relapsing; H. pylori eradication and removing NSAIDs usually resolve symptoms; a minority progress to ulcer or (with chronic atrophic gastritis) increased gastric cancer risk.
overview.prognosis: Good; depends on cause and on excluding serious pathology.

prevalence.value: Very common; dyspepsia affects a large proportion of adults at some point. H. pylori is highly prevalent worldwide.

incidence.value: High; NSAID use and H. pylori are major drivers.

mortality.value: Low directly; relevant via bleeding or underlying malignancy.

epidemiology.geographic_distribution: Worldwide; H. pylori prevalence higher in many low/middle-income regions.

risk_factors.smoking: Impairs mucosal healing; increases ulcer/cancer risk.
risk_factors.travel: H. pylori acquisition in endemic areas.
risk_factors.family_history: H. pylori clustering; family history of gastric cancer (a red flag).
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Peptic ulcer disease, prior H. pylori, autoimmune conditions (pernicious anaemia).

symptoms.symptom: Symptoms related to NSAID use / relieved by antacids
Weight loss / progressive dysphagia / persistent vomiting

negative_findings.finding: No alarm features (bleeding, dysphagia, weight loss, persistent vomiting, mass, anaemia)
negative_findings.why_important: Supports empirical management without urgent endoscopy
Consider a cardiac cause of epigastric pain (do not miss)

history_questions.question: Where is the pain, and is it related to meals, NSAIDs, or relieved by antacids?
Any black stools, vomiting blood, difficulty swallowing, weight loss, or persistent vomiting?
Do you take NSAIDs/aspirin, and how much alcohol?
Any family history of gastric cancer or prior peptic ulcer/H. pylori?
Is the pain ever brought on by exertion (cardiac)?
history_questions.why_ask: Do not miss cardiac epigastric pain

physical_examination.expected_finding: Epigastric tenderness; usually otherwise normal (a mass is a red flag)

physical_examination.examination: Cardiovascular assessment if pain could be cardiac

laboratory_tests.test_name: H. pylori testing (stool antigen or urea breath test)
laboratory_tests.indication: Test-and-treat in uncomplicated dyspepsia (stop PPI before testing for accuracy)

imaging.when_needed: Not first-line (endoscopy is the relevant investigation)

ecg.when_needed: If epigastric pain could be cardiac
ecg.findings: Used to help exclude cardiac ischaemia.

other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: Upper GI endoscopy for alarm features, age/risk-based new dyspepsia, or treatment failure; may show gastritis/erosions/ulcer/malignancy; allows biopsy for H. pylori/atrophy/dysplasia.
other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: Gastric biopsy at endoscopy (H. pylori, atrophy, dysplasia, malignancy)

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Uninvestigated dyspepsia/gastritis is a clinical diagnosis managed per pathway (NICE CG184): exclude alarm features, review drugs/lifestyle, then H. pylori test-and-treat and/or a PPI trial. Endoscopy defines gastritis/erosions histologically when performed.

differential_diagnosis.differences: May have distinct hunger/night pain; ulcer on endoscopy
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is the pain relieved by food or worse at night?
Is it mainly heartburn/acid coming up?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Alarm features - weight loss, dysphagia, anaemia, mass, older age
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any weight loss, trouble swallowing, or vomiting blood?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Cardiac ischaemia / biliary or pancreatic disease
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is it exertional, or right-sided radiating to the back?

diagnostic_questions.question: Any black stools, vomiting blood, difficulty swallowing, weight loss, or a lump?

next_best_question.question: Any alarm features, NSAID use, and would you prefer test-and-treat for H. pylori or a PPI trial?
next_best_question.expected_answers: No alarm features -> empirical; alarm features -> endoscopy
next_best_question.branching_logic: No alarm features -> stop NSAIDs, H. pylori test-and-treat and/or PPI; alarm features/older new dyspepsia -> urgent endoscopy

red_flags.immediate_action: Urgent/emergency assessment for upper GI bleeding

red_flags.finding: Dysphagia, weight loss, persistent vomiting, epigastric mass, or iron-deficiency anaemia
Severe sudden epigastric pain with peritonitis (perforation)

referral_criteria.routine_referral: Refractory symptoms despite eradication/PPI; diagnostic uncertainty.

late: Increased gastric cancer risk (chronic H. pylori/atrophy)

initial_management.supportive_care: Explain the condition; review and stop NSAIDs where possible; lifestyle advice.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Proton-pump inhibitor; H. pylori eradication regimen; NSAID withdrawal/substitution. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG184, ACG_HPYLORI_2024.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Reduce alcohol, stop smoking, avoid trigger foods, weight management if reflux overlap.
initial_management.follow_up: Review response; retest/confirm eradication where indicated; endoscopy if not improving or new alarm features.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Stop/limit NSAIDs, alcohol; proton-pump inhibitor for symptom control; H. pylori eradication (triple/quadric therapy per local resistance) if positive - confirm eradication for ulcers/where indicated. Antacids/alginates for symptom relief.

patient_education.home_advice: Gastritis/indigestion is irritation of the stomach lining, often from a bacterium (H. pylori) or anti-inflammatory painkillers (NSAIDs). Stopping NSAIDs, cutting alcohol, and acid-reducing tablets usually help; if H. pylori is found, a short course of antibiotics clears it. See a doctor promptly if you vomit blood, pass black tarry stools, have trouble swallowing, or lose weight.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: التهاب المعدة/عسر الهضم تهيّج في بطانة المعدة، غالباً من جرثومة (الملوية البوابية) أو مسكّنات مضادة للالتهاب (NSAIDs). يفيد إيقاف هذه المسكّنات وتقليل الكحول وأدوية تقليل الحمض؛ وإن وُجدت الجرثومة فجرعة قصيرة من المضادات تقضي عليها. راجع الطبيب سريعاً إذا تقيّأت دماً، أو نزل براز أسود قطراني، أو صعُب البلع، أو نقص وزنك.
patient_education.prevention: Avoid unnecessary NSAIDs (use gastroprotection if needed), limit alcohol, treat H. pylori.
patient_education.warning_signs: Vomiting blood, black stools, difficulty swallowing, weight loss, or severe/persistent pain.

prevention.lifestyle: Limit NSAIDs/alcohol; H. pylori eradication where indicated.
prevention.screening: Not applicable (surveillance for high-risk premalignant gastric changes per specialist).

evidence.evidence_level: High for H. pylori eradication and PPI therapy; strong for alarm-feature-based endoscopy.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_CG184, ACG_HPYLORI_2024; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Treat the cause, protect mucosa and eradicate confirmed H. pylori using resistance-aware therapy.

Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Proton-pump inhibitor; H. pylori eradication regimen; NSAID withdrawal/substitution. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG184, ACG_HPYLORI_2024.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
H. pylori test and prior therapy
non_drug_measures: Reduce alcohol/smoking and review irritating medicines; do not assume every dyspeptic symptom is gastritis.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Symptomatic/erosive disease or gastroprotection when indicated
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

use_caution_if: long-term use, osteoporosis risk, low magnesium/B12/iron, C. difficile risk, severe liver disease, or clopidogrel interaction for some PPIs
monitoring: response and ongoing indication; magnesium/B12/iron or bone risk when clinically indicated

medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

use_caution_if: penicillin allergy, pregnancy, QT risk, liver/renal disease, prior macrolide/fluoroquinolone exposure, or anticoagulation
monitoring: adherence/adverse effects and mandatory test of cure using an accepted method after the recommended washout

avoid_if: active gastrointestinal bleeding/ulcer, serious NSAID allergy, or NSAID-triggered asthma
use_caution_if: chronic kidney disease, heart failure, hypertension, anticoagulation/antiplatelet therapy, older age, pregnancy, or dehydration
monitoring: renal function, blood pressure, oedema and gastrointestinal bleeding symptoms when clinically indicated

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Urgent care/endoscopy for bleeding, anaemia, weight loss, persistent vomiting, severe pain/peritonism or cancer risk.
